topic.title: SIPRI Report: India as 2nd Largest Arms Importer

subtopics.title: SIPRI and global arms transfers
subtopics.summary: The Stockholm International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI), an independent research institute, released the Trends in International Arms Transfers 2025 report on global defence trade. International arms transfers rose 9.2% in 2021-25 compared with 2016-20. The rise in European arms imports, up 210%, was largely driven by the Russia-Ukraine war.

SIPRI headquarters: Stockholm, Sweden

subtopics.title: Top global exporters and importers
subtopics.summary: The SIPRI report ranks the largest arms exporters and importers for 2021-25. The United States led exports with a 42% share, while Ukraine topped imports with a 9.7% share. Russia's arms exports fell sharply, cutting its share of global exports.

subtopics.title: India as 2nd largest arms importer
subtopics.summary: India remained the second-largest arms importer during 2021-25, with an 8.2% share. Its overall arms imports fell by 4%, largely due to increased domestic defence manufacturing and indigenisation. Russia, France and Israel were its main suppliers.

subtopics.title: India's push for domestic defence
subtopics.summary: India has set production and export targets for 2029 and is building its domestic defence capacity. Policy changes, defence industrial corridors and foreign investment rules support this aim. The top three export destinations are the US, France and Armenia.

quizzes.title: Global arms transfers quiz
quizzes.passage: International arms transfers are the movement of weapons and military equipment from one country to another, and they show how global defence trade is changing. The Stockholm International Peace Research Institute, an independent research body that studies conflict and peace, armaments, military expenditure and disarmament, examined these transfers in its Trends in International Arms Transfers 2025 report. The report analysed the period from 2021 to 2025 and compared it with the earlier five-year period from 2016 to 2020, which allows changes in global defence trade to be measured over time. Its findings show that overall transfers grew between the two periods. The increase was particularly strong in Europe, where arms imports rose sharply, and the institute linked much of this surge to the Russia-Ukraine war. Trade patterns also shifted among suppliers, as one major exporter saw its shipments fall significantly and its share of global exports became much smaller. The report offers a picture of which countries supply weapons to the world and which countries buy them. Such information helps observers understand how the balance of global defence trade is moving.

quizzes.title: India's arms imports quiz
quizzes.passage: India has long been one of the largest buyers of defence equipment in the world, and its purchases shape both its military capability and its relationships with foreign suppliers. In the most recent SIPRI assessment, covering 2021 to 2025, India kept a high position among the world's arms importers. However, its total arms imports during this period were lower than in the earlier phase, a change linked to a growing push for domestic production. Over the past several years, the government has focused on building a stronger defence manufacturing base at home. Procurement policy was revised to prioritise Indian-made products over foreign purchases, which signals a clear preference for local industry. To support this shift, industrial corridors have been created in certain states to bring together manufacturers and suppliers. Foreign investment is also allowed in the defence sector through both automatic and government routes, while a dedicated initiative supports start-ups and small firms working on innovation. Taken together, these steps aim to reduce dependence on imported weapons and to turn India into a larger producer and exporter of defence equipment.
